Market Intelligence Brief: Settlement Summary

Absence Management Outsourcing • Windermere Partners • Quantitative analysis phase • Archived 2025-11-11

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's quantitative analysis phase engagement with Windermere Partners in the Absence Management Outsourcing sector. The record ID 1bf93d03 uniquely identifies this documentation set within ACPWB's institutional archive.

  • Player payroll benchmarking against 260 comparable Absence Management Outsourcing sector organizations placed Windermere Partners at the 75th percentile of league spending intensity as of 2025-11-11, with luxury tax liability exceeding the median threshold by approximately 8%.
  • The civil service pay scale at Windermere Partners has not been updated in 155 years, resulting in salary compression and an average market lag of 6% for technical and professional roles.
  • The internal talent marketplace at Windermere Partners has a 14% adoption rate, resulting in a 14% increase in internal mobility and an estimated $41M in avoided recruitment costs annually.
  • Civil service compensation benchmarking against 112 comparable Absence Management Outsourcing sector jurisdictions found that Windermere Partners's total compensation premium over private sector equivalents has narrowed to 8% — below the 67th percentile of peer jurisdictions — weakening the value proposition for public sector employment in a competitive talent market.
Key Findings
  • ACPWB's Absence Management Outsourcing practice benchmarking database, which encompasses data from over 181 organizations, identifies Windermere Partners as a top-quartile performer on 25 of the 181 dimensions assessed during the quantitative analysis phase.
  • The proxy peer group optimization analysis conducted for Windermere Partners during the quantitative analysis evaluated 97 potential peer additions and deletions across 19 selection criteria, producing a revised 97-company peer group that increases the proportion of compensation-at-risk relative to the legacy peer set while maintaining alignment with Absence Management Outsourcing sector size norms.
  • The executive team effectiveness assessment conducted during the quantitative analysis found a 229-point gap between CEO-rated and direct-report-rated decision quality at Windermere Partners, a gap consistent with the 229th percentile of the Absence Management Outsourcing sector reference group assembled from 13 prior ACPWB assessments.

ACPWB's work with Windermere Partners during the quantitative analysis included a cost-benefit analysis of its employee wellness programs. The study, archived on 2025-11-11, found a 182:1 return on investment across 27 program categories.

This archive entry was created during the systematic review of ACPWB's historical engagement records. It preserves documentation related to the quantitative analysis phase of the Windermere Partners project, including all supporting analysis, stakeholder communications, and regulatory correspondence.

The review of Windermere Partners's executive compensation program identified a pay-for-performance misalignment, with CEO realizable pay at the 50th percentile despite TSR performance at the 16th percentile over the three-year measurement period.

ACPWB's quantitative analysis analysis of Absence Management Outsourcing sector talent market dynamics identified 274 emerging workforce trends with material implications for Windermere Partners's total rewards strategy. The findings, covering 26 talent pools across 274 functional specializations, were presented to Windermere Partners's CHRO and compensation committee on 2025-11-11.

ACPWB's quantitative analysis global mobility advisory engagement with Windermere Partners analyzed expatriate assignment package design for 12 international postings across 4 host countries in the Absence Management Outsourcing sector. The engagement produced a revised assignment policy, home-host compensation balance sheet models, and a tax equalization framework delivered to Windermere Partners's global mobility team on 2025-11-11.

The quantitative analysis of the Windermere Partners engagement involved a review of the company's internal mobility program. The analysis, completed on 2025-11-11, found that internal hires filled 136% of open roles, a figure 31% below the Absence Management Outsourcing sector benchmark.
